_source: Transcribed from the QCTO documents for SAQA qualification 121150,
Higher Occupational Certificate: Human Resource Management Administrator:
PARTIAL. Every module is here with its official code, title and credits.
Only KM01 has been transcribed down to topics, topic elements and internal
assessment criteria — it is a worked example of the shape, not a complete
curriculum. Readiness reports curriculumComplete: false and refuses to call
anybody EISA eligible until the remaining twelve modules are transcribed.
Note on KM01's credits: the curriculum document's module list says 4 and its
detail heading says 12. The qualification record says 4, and 4 is what makes
the Knowledge component add up to its stated 42. Taken as 4; the heading
appears to be an error in the source document.
title: Higher Occupational Certificate: Human Resource Management Administrator
_componentWeights: The curriculum document states these percentages directly, under 'Summary
and Distribution of Credits'. They are not the credit split — credits give
35/35/30 — and the document is what a moderator checks against.
_exitLevelOutcomes: From the SAQA qualification document: the four Exit Level Outcomes and
their Associated Assessment Criteria. The EISA is set against these; the
IACs inside modules are what the provider assesses internally.

exitLevelOutcomes.description: Collect Human Resources data and process the data into appropriate information that is available for decision-making.
criteria: Use appropriate information technology to collect HRM data that is required for specific HRM tasks and processes.
Validate, analyse, and convert collected HRM data into information that is reported for HRM decision-making.
Prepare and present appropriate presentations at meetings, stakeholders and to diverse groups of decision-makers.
Maintain HRM databases, and extract appropriate information in response to specific authorised requests.

exitLevelOutcomes.description: Select and use appropriate methods, techniques, and procedures to provide professional administrative services for the full range of HRM processes and activities.
criteria: Provide administrative services for Workforce Planning in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.
Provide administrative services for Staff Recruitment, Selection and Placement in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.
Provide administrative services for Performance Management in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.
Provide administrative services for employee Learning and Development in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.
Provide administrative services for Grievance and Discipline Handling in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.
Provide administrative services for Career Management in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.
Provide administrative services for all Staff Separations in an ethical and legally compliant way that is aligned with HRM professional standards.

exitLevelOutcomes.description: Monitor, support and maintain the various communication and administrative processes with relevant stakeholders to optimise the employment relations in the organisation.
criteria: Update and maintain information systems relating to all HRM policies, procedures, and legislative requirements.
Maintain, update, and make accessible approved HRM policy guideline documents to relevant organisational stakeholders.
Maintain and make available records of regular and ad hoc employee meetings and forums to authorised persons in the organisation.
Receive, record and respond to employee queries relating to policies, procedures, and related employment contractual issues appropriately.
Official HRM communication channels are coordinated and maintained within the organisation.

exitLevelOutcomes.description: Access and use appropriate HRM systems and processes for the compilation, maintenance and safeguarding of all HRM records.
criteria: Compile and maintain HRM records, including personal employee records.
Control and manage access to information in employee and HRM records.
Archive and retrieve employee and HRM records effectively as needed.

_studyUnits: The provider's delivery structure, from STEP 1 - CA - 121150 - KM PM ELO
Alignment. Each study unit bundles the Knowledge, Practical and Work
Experience modules serving one Exit Level Outcome. Study Unit 1 serves
none: it is an introduction carrying credits but aligned to no ELO.

modules.title: Introduction to Organisations and Human Resource Management
modules.purpose: To build an informed base of knowledge and understanding of the theories, concepts and principles that underpin the basic operations of organisations, with specific reference to the HRM function.

elements.description: Definition of an organisation and the generic organisational value chain.
Different types of organisations and their purpose.
The concept of staff, line, and professional work in organisations.
Definition of management and the functions and activities of management.
Introduction to the different levels of management in organisations (Strategic, Functional, Tactical and Operational).
Introduction to an ecosystemic approach to organisational sustainability.

criteria.description: Define an organisation and explain the generic organisational value chain.
Identify different types of organisations and explain their purpose.
Define management and discuss the functions and activities of management.
Differentiate the different levels of management in organisations (Strategic, Functional, Tactical and Operational).
Explain the ecosystemic approach to organisational sustainability.

elements.description: Brief overview of the origin, history, and evolution of HRM.
The typical employment life cycle and the associated HRM value chain.
Introduction to the legislative framework that governs and guides the work in HRM.
The importance of data and data management within the HRM function.

criteria.description: Summarise the origin, history, and evolution of HRM.
Explain the typical employment life cycle and the associated HRM value chain.
Discuss the legislative framework that governs and guides the work in HRM.
Define data and explain data management within the HRM function.

topics.title: The use of information in organisations

elements.description: Definitions and terms associated with data, data collection and data processing.
Importance of data and data collection within organisations.
The evolving concept of the information economy and how it impacts data management.
Legislative and ethical issues relating to data management.

criteria.description: Define terms associated with data, data collection and data processing.
Discuss the importance of data and data collection within organisations.
Explain the evolving concept of the information economy and how it impacts data management.
List legislative and indicate ethical issues relating to data management.

topics.title: Administration and the administrative role in HRM

elements.description: Definitions, terms and concepts associated with administration.
The difference between clerical and administrative work.
The functions and activities of an office administrator.
The role and importance of good administration within the HRM function.
Key abilities, attributes and professional standards that underpin the work of a HRM administrator.

criteria.description: Define terms and concepts associated with administration.
Differentiate between clerical and administrative work.
List the functions and activities of an office administrator.
Discuss the role and importance of good administration within the HRM function.
Discuss the essential abilities, attributes and professional standards that underpin the work of a HRM administrator.
